likelyComponents: STAGE draining / water remains — pump / filter
STAGE stuck on drying — heater / airflow
STAGE random stop — power / door / control
discriminators: Identify WHICH stage it sticks at first — that decides the suspect.

likelyComponents: property socket / supply / fused spur (test with another appliance)
diverter stuck (only upper OR lower arm ever runs)
discriminators: If only one spray arm ever gets water, suspect the diverter before the circulation pump.

likelyComponents: dirty sensor lens / debris in the sump (clean first)

discriminators: Water in the base with an overfill error: check the float and a passing inlet valve.
Intermittent or multi-error faults on a dishwasher are very often the flexing door wiring loom.

likelyComponents: dust / blockage on the condenser and fan (clean first)
door seal / gasket (perished, warped or dirty)
discriminators: Condensation, icing or over-working compressor is often just a poor door seal — check it seals on paper first.

likelyComponents: water supply / stop tap / house pressure

discriminators: One compartment wrong temperature while the other is fine points at the air damper.

likelyComponents: door left open / poor door seal (warm alarm)
actual compartment temperatures (is it genuinely warm?)
STOP USE and isolate at the socket if there is burning, scorching or a smell of hot plastic (safety first)
compressor start relay / overload (electrical fault as it tries to start)
mains lead / plug / internal wiring or connector
discriminators: A fridge-freezer that trips the electrics/RCD is an EARTH-LEAKAGE or short-circuit electrical fault - it is NOT a cooling-performance question, so do not lead with 'compressor failed' or 'needs re-gassing'. Use the TIMING as evidence, not proof: trips the INSTANT it is plugged in / switched on => mains lead, plug, incoming wiring or a dead short; trips when the COMPRESSOR tries to start (a click/hum every few minutes then a trip) => the start relay/overload or the compressor windings leaking to earth; trips after running a while => wiring/connector or compressor insulation breaking down as it warms.

A cold fridge that suddenly trips, with a burning or hot-plastic smell or visible scorching at the plug/socket or the back, is an electrical safety fault - STOP USE and isolate. Do not keep resetting the RCD to see if it holds.

SAFETY: do NOT tell the customer to insulation-test, energise or probe live components, open the sealed refrigeration system, work on the compressor terminals, bypass the earth or RCD, or repeatedly reset the trip. Sealed-system and live electrical work is for a qualified engineer only.

commonConfusion.name: tripping = compressor failed / needs re-gassing
commonConfusion.note: Tripping the RCD is an EARTH FAULT (relay, compressor insulation, wiring or the mains lead), not a refrigerant/gas charge issue and not automatically a dead compressor. Locate the electrical fault safely; a re-gas is never the answer to a trip.
wouldApplyIf: the fridge trips the electrics or RCD

commonConfusion.name: keeps tripping = just reset it
commonConfusion.note: Repeated tripping is the protection doing its job on a real fault. Repeatedly resetting the RCD or moving it to another socket to 'keep it going' is unsafe - stop use and have the electrical fault found.
wouldApplyIf: the customer is resetting the trip to keep using it

adviceBeforeReplacement: note exactly when it trips - on plug-in, when the compressor tries to start, or after running
stop repeatedly resetting the RCD and isolate the appliance if there is any burning smell or scorching
keep the freezer closed to protect the food while the fault is found
fridge-freezer:tripping-electrics.safety: SAFETY (authoritative): a fridge-freezer that trips the electrics has an electrical fault (earth leakage or short) somewhere in the mains lead, wiring, start relay or compressor. Do NOT tell the customer to insulation-test, energise or probe live parts, work on the compressor terminals, open the sealed refrigeration/refrigerant system, bypass the earth or RCD, or repeatedly reset the trip. A burning smell, scorching or smoke => STOP USE and isolate at the socket/spur. Sealed-system and live electrical work is for a qualified engineer only.

mediaInformation.description: When a hob zone won't heat or heats unevenly, the parts involved are the heating element/zone, the temperature sensor and the control board — and on an induction hob, the pan itself must be suitable. This reference shows where they sit and the safe checks (use the right pan, keep the surface clean, try a reset). Replacing hob parts is a job for a qualified engineer.

likelyComponents: identify hob type first (ceramic radiant / solid plate / induction)
radiant element or solid hotplate for the affected zone
discriminators: The part depends on hob type and which zones fail: one dead zone on a ceramic/solid hob is that element or its switch; on induction it is the coil/power module (see power-module).

likelyComponents: confirm it is an induction hob
induction coil / generator for the affected zone
discriminators: One induction zone dead = its coil or power module; ALL zones dead = shared power board, supply or a fan/overheat shutdown.

likelyComponents: water / spillage / wet cloth on the panel (clean and dry first)
discriminators: Erratic or dead touch controls are very often just moisture on the glass — dry it before condemning parts.
No spark on all burners = ignition switch/module; one burner = that electrode or a dirty/wet burner cap.

likelyComponents: cracked ceramic / glass hob top — replace the glass top (stop using it until repaired)
discriminators: A cracked hob surface is a safety issue (shock/spillage into live parts) — stop use until the glass is replaced.

likelyComponents: STOP USE and isolate at the fused spur/consumer unit if there is burning, scorching or a smell of hot plastic (safety first)
moisture / spillage tracking under the ceramic glass (dry out first where accessible)
radiant or solid element leaking to earth (ceramic / solid-plate hobs)
induction coil / power module leaking to earth (induction hobs)
mains wiring / connection block at the hob
discriminators: ARCHITECTURE FIRST: a hob that trips the electrics/RCD is an EARTH-LEAKAGE fault, but where it lives depends on the hob type. CERAMIC/SOLID-PLATE => most often a radiant/solid ELEMENT leaking to earth, or moisture/spillage tracking under the glass; INDUCTION => the induction COIL or POWER MODULE / generator, or its wiring. Do not apply element reasoning to an induction hob or induction-module reasoning to a ceramic hob.

Use TIMING/ZONE as evidence, not proof: trips the instant it is switched on => incoming wiring/connection or a dead short; trips only when a particular ZONE is turned up => that zone's element/coil leaking (but shared wiring can mislead, so it is not absolute); trips after a spill or clean => moisture ingress under the glass. Let the hob dry fully before condemning a part when a spill preceded it.

SAFETY: repeated tripping, or any burning/scorching/hot-plastic smell => STOP USE and isolate at the fused spur/consumer unit (hobs are usually wired in, not plugged). Do NOT tell the customer to insulation-test, energise or probe live parts, work on induction power electronics (which hold a dangerous charge), bypass the earth/RCD, or repeatedly reset the trip.

commonConfusion.name: induction trip = power module (always) / ceramic trip = element (always)
commonConfusion.note: Identify the hob technology before naming a part. A trip on a ceramic/solid hob is usually an element or moisture under the glass; on induction it is the coil/power module or wiring. Naming the wrong architecture's part is a mis-diagnosis.
wouldApplyIf: the hob trips the electrics and the technology has not been established

commonConfusion.name: keeps tripping = just reset it
commonConfusion.note: Repeated tripping is the protection responding to a real earth fault. Repeatedly resetting the breaker/RCD to keep cooking is unsafe - stop use and have the fault found.
wouldApplyIf: the customer is resetting the trip to keep using the hob

adviceBeforeReplacement: establish whether it is a ceramic, solid-plate or induction hob
note when it trips - on switch-on, on a particular zone, or after a spill/clean
if a spill or clean preceded it, let the hob dry fully before assuming a failed part
stop using it and isolate at the spur if there is any burning smell or scorching
hobs:tripping-electrics.safety: SAFETY (authoritative): a hob that trips the electrics has an earth-leakage/short fault (element, induction coil/power module, moisture ingress or wiring). Do NOT tell the customer to insulation-test, energise or probe live parts, open or work on induction power electronics (they can hold a dangerous charge), bypass the earth/RCD, or repeatedly reset the trip. Hobs are usually wired to a fused spur - isolate there. A burning smell, scorching or smoke => STOP USE. Live electrical work is for a qualified engineer only.

thermal cut-out on the brush motor

discriminators: Totally dead points to the power supply: on a corded model the cable, plug fuse or on/off switch; on a cordless model the battery and charger first. Only suspect the motor once these are ruled out.
